title: Motive and reciprocal inducement
summary: Generosity and other motives can coexist with a bargain; the requested exchange still must be identified.
notes: The text’s discussion of Restatement § 81 and Holmes’s reciprocal inducement formulation distinguishes why a party desires an outcome from the act requested as its price. A promise made partly from affection may remain bargained for. Conversely, reliance or a benefit occurring without being sought in exchange does not become consideration merely because it helps explain the transaction.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 58–61. Open assigned page 58.
